item.title: [planForChange] Discover usage-based billing (UBB) experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot
item.description:
[What and why:]

As previously announced in MC1479277, we are making usage-based experiences in the Microsoft Copilot app easier to discover. Usage-based billing experiences like Cowork, Code, and Autopilot, will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, even if their organization has not enabled access. Users without an applicable spending policy will see an option to request access or learn more, based on their organization's settings.

Based on customer feedback, we are extending the rollout timeline and introducing an additional admin control that will allow organizations to provide custom guidance to users. These changes give administrators more time to prepare and greater flexibility to manage how users discover and request access to usage-based experiences.

[Rollout schedule:]

The updated rollout schedule is as follows:

  • Mid-November 2026: The new admin setting, "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences," will become available for administrators to configure.
  • Mid-December 2026: An additional option will be introduced to the admin setting, allowing administrators to provide a custom URL as part of the Learn more informational experience that directs users to their own organization’s guidance. The option will be available if you select "Specific users" or “No users” in the setting.
  • End of January 2027: The new discoverability behavior and admin setting will be enforced. The old setting "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing" will be retired. This will apply to customers on deferred release at the end of February 2027.

[Impact on your organization:]

Who is affected: 

  • Organizations with users licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Platforms/services: 

  • Microsoft Copilot app and Microsoft 365 admin center.

What will happen:

  • Entry points for Cowork, Code, and Autopilot will be visible by default to licensed users starting at the end of January 2027.
  • Users without an applicable spending policy giving them access to the feature will see an informational experience with an option to "Request access" or "Learn more," depending on their how their organization has configured the new "Access requests to usage-based billing experiences" admin setting.
  • Administrators can configure which users are eligible to request access, including the option to prevent access requests.
  • Administrators will be able to provide a custom URL directing users to organizational guidance. Only users who cannot request access will see the secondary URL, "Your organization’s guidance", as part of the Learn more informational experience.  
  • The existing setting, "Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing," will continue to apply until it is retired at the end of January 2027.

Examples of the customizable “Your organization’s guidance” link on the informational experience for Cowork and Code. UI subject to change.

This change does not automatically enable usage-based experiences or initiate billing. Users must have an applicable spending policy and available Copilot Credits before they can use these experiences.

[Action required / recommendations:]

We recommend that administrators:

  1. Review the new setting in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings > Access requests to usage-based billing experiences when it becomes available in mid-November. Starting mid-December, you will be able to configure a custom URL in this setting for users who you decide cannot request access.
  2. Configure access request preferences to determine which users can request access to usage-based experiences.
  3. Prepare organizational guidance and, beginning in mid-December, configure a custom URL if you want to direct users to information specific to your organization.
  4. Review spending policies to ensure that access to usage-based experiences aligns with your organization's requirements.

We recommend reviewing and configuring these settings before the new discoverability behavior is enforced at the end of January 2027.

Learn more: Access requests to usage-based billing experiences (This will be updated in mid-Dec to reflect instructions for the custom URL once available in the setting)

[Compliance considerations:]

This update introduces additional administrative controls for managing access requests and organizational guidance. It does not automatically grant users access to usage-based experiences or change existing spending policy requirements.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Classic Outlook for Windows: Upcoming visual improvements and a more consistent Outlook experience
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We’ve heard your feedback that you’d like more information about what’s changing in classic Outlook. To help end-users understand recent changes, we’re bringing back the What’s New in-app dialog. 

The dialog is designed to be nonintrusive and will appear automatically at most once per month in Production on Current Channel. Users can dismiss it at any time and reopen it later by selecting the What’s New button on the ribbon. Administrators can turn off the automated dialog and hide its ribbon button. 

For more information and configuration instructions, see What’s New in classic Outlook for Windows.

[What and why]

We’re making updates across Microsoft Outlook experiences to improve clarity and consistency across endpoints. The first updates focus on visual details such as icons, spacing, and alignment, while maintaining familiar ways of working.

These updates are part of an ongoing series of improvements across Outlook experiences and are not a replacement for the classic Outlook experience.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by late November 2026

  • The initial visual updates will roll out to classic Outlook Current Channel. Users may receive individual improvements at different times as the rollout progresses.
  • We will provide additional advance notice before larger changes that might affect navigation or workflows, including timing and any preparation required.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users of classic Outlook for Windows Current Channel

Platforms and services

  • The initial visual updates apply to classic Outlook for Windows Current Channel.
  • We are also improving Outlook on the web, new Outlook for Windows, and Outlook for macOS to reduce unnecessary differences and make familiar capabilities easier to recognize across devices.

What will happen

  • Users will begin seeing visual refinements to familiar mail and calendar surfaces, including updates to icons, spacing, and alignment.
  • These initial updates are intended to improve clarity and consistency without changing how users perform their tasks.
  • This change does not replace the classic Outlook experience.
  • No admin configuration changes are required for these initial visual updates.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform your help desk that the appearance of some Outlook controls may change as updates roll out.
  • Inform users as appropriate.
  • Continue to direct users to Outlook’s existing feedback options to share feedback.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform admin center - Connector inventory in Power Platform inventory
item.description:
We are announcing Connector inventory in Power Platform inventory. This feature will reach general availability by November 10, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Connector inventory makes common admin workflows query-driven, identifying every resource affected by a deprecated connector, tracking Premium connector adoption for license decisions, scoping DLP policies to actual usage patterns, and reviewing a resource's full connector footprint during troubleshooting.

In the Power Platform admin center, a Connectors column appears across the inventory grids: the unified Manage > Inventory page and the resource-specific views under Copilot Studio, Power Apps, and Power Automate. The same data is available programmatically through the Power Platform for Admins V2 connector, the Power Platform inventory API, Power Platform CLI, and Azure Resource Graph, so you can build reports and automate governance.

What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Connector inventory Connector inventory.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Pay-as-you-go consumption-based meter for your extra SharePoint storage needs
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

To help organizations manage SharePoint storage more flexibly and avoid over-provisioning, Microsoft is introducing a pay-as-you-go, consumption-based billing model for SharePoint storage overages. This option allows you to pay only for the additional storage you actually use, rather than pre-purchasing extra capacity. The experience integrates with Microsoft 365 Archive and helps align storage costs with real usage.

This change is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 506743.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): We completed rollout in June 2026.
  • General Availability (WW): We expect to begin rolling out in early January 2027 (previously early November) and to complete rolling by late January 2027 (previously end of November). 

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Microsoft 365 administrators managing SharePoint Online storage
  • Note: This feature isn’t currently available to education tenants. Let us know if you’d like it to be supported in the future.

What will happen:

  • Admins can enable pay-as-you-go SharePoint storage billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Storage used above the included tenant quota will be automatically billed based on consumption.
  • There is no impact to users.
  • The existing Office 365 Extra File Storage add‑on remains available if you prefer to manually increase your storage quota instead.
  • The feature is opt-in and off by default.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No immediate action is required. However, we recommend the following:
  • Review your tenant’s current SharePoint storage usage in the SharePoint admin center > Active sites.
  • Evaluate whether a consumption‑based model or manually purchased storage best fits your organization’s cost and governance preferences.
  • If you plan to enable pay‑as‑you‑go billing:
    • Ensure the appropriate Azure subscription and billing permissions are in place.
    • Update internal documentation or cost‑management processes as needed.
  • Share this information with finance or procurement teams if they track usage‑based charges.

Learn more: Add more SharePoint storage to your subscription | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance areaImpact and explanation
Admin monitoring and reportingSharePoint storage usage above the included tenant quota will be reflected in consumption-based billing and usage reports, which may affect how admins monitor and track storage consumption and costs.
Admin controlAdministrators must explicitly enable

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the rollout scope and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI through a user subscription license with Advanced AI through usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, 2026, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants. This phased approach makes it easier for new customers to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs. 

This change will not apply to your existing Microsoft 365 tenant as part of the November rollout. We will share additional information before making usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants. If you’d like to get started sooner, you can enable usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

What is changing 

  • Eligible purchases made by new tenants: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and Microsoft 365 Business with Copilot purchases made by new tenants. 
  • If the new tenant does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy, they will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month, with charges based on actual usage. 
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by the administrator. 
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, the Netherlands, Poland, or Spain. We plan to include these markets in the next phase of the rollout in early 2027, with additional details and timing to be shared closer to launch. 

What is not changing 

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Usage-based billing will not be configured by default for your existing tenant as part of the November rollout. 
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place. 

When this will happen 

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made by new tenants directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web. 
  • Existing tenants: We plan to make usage-based billing easier to enable for existing tenants across all markets beginning in early 2027. We’ll share more details, including specific timing and what to expect, closer to launch. 
  • Optional action: Existing tenants can turn on usage-based billing at any time through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Starting in early 2027: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels, with specific timing to be shared closer to launch. 

How usage-based billing works 

  • When usage-based billing is configured, the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and spending policy support access to eligible usage-based experiences. 
  • If you want to turn on usage-based billing for your existing tenant, you can create and manage a spending policy through Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  • Your organization can adjust its spending policies and controls to align with its needs. Disabling usage-based billing prevents access to experiences that require it. 

What you can do to prepare 

  • Review which eligible usage-based experiences—including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities—may support your organization’s needs. 
  • Review your organization’s usage-based billing, governance, and cost-management requirements. 
  • If you choose to turn on usage-based billing ahead of this update, you can create or adjust usage controls and spending policies in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 

Learn more 

  • Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center: https://admin.cloud.microsoft/#/copilot/costmanagement/overview 
  • Usage-based billing and cost management for Copilot Credits: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits 
  • Cloud Based Billing: What is a cloud subscription? - Microsoft Cost Management | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Purview: permissions audit log improvements
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

To improve transparency and troubleshooting for Microsoft Purview role-based access control (RBAC), we are enhancing audit logging for permission checks performed in the Microsoft Purview portal. These new audit records will provide administrators with clearer visibility into role and scoped-role authorization decisions, helping them investigate access issues and better understand how access evaluations are performed.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 569363.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators and compliance administrators who review audit logs for access investigations and troubleshooting

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview portal
  • Microsoft Purview Audit

What will happen

  • New audit records will be generated when access checks are performed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
  • Two new audit operations will be available:
    • CheckUsersInRoles
    • CheckUserInRolesWithScopes
  • Administrators will be able to review these audit records as part of SecurityComplianceRBAC audit activities.
  • The enhancement is enabled by default and requires no configuration.
  • Audit records will only be generated for access checks that occur after the feature is deployed.
  • No historical or retroactive audit records will be created for prior access checks.
  • There is no impact for organizations.
  • Supported permission-assignment and role-group change audit records will include the ClientPortal field within PreExecutionMessage, helping administrators distinguish changes initiated from Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender. 
    • Supported activities for portal attribution 
      • Permission assignments: Granting, updating, or removing permission assignments. 
      • Role groups: Creating, updating, or deleting role groups. 
  • Expected ClientPortal values: 
    • Microsoft Purview portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Purview" 
    • Microsoft Defender portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Defender" 

RBAC audit-CheckUserInRolesWithScopes:

RBAC audit-checkusersinroles:

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that administrators:

  • Review internal monitoring and audit procedures to determine whether the new audit activities should be included in access investigations.
  • Inform compliance and security teams about the availability of the new audit operations.
  • Update any internal documentation or reporting processes that reference Microsoft Purview RBAC audit data.

Learn more

  • Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable audit logging capabilities?Yes. The change enhances audit logging capabilities by adding two new audit operations.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators gain additional audit visibility into RBAC access evaluation outcomes, improving monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026 and is expected to complete by end of December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Legal plugins in Word and Cowork
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft 365 Copilot is introducing legal plugins in Word and Cowork. These plugins provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents. They can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources, helping legal professionals complete legal work in the Microsoft 365 experiences they already use.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout began in late April 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-October 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot commercial licenses

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Word desktop
  • Cowork

What will happen

  • Legal plugins in Copilot provide purpose-built skills to help legal professionals summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
  • The plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 and connect to supported third-party legal sources.
  • The legal capabilities include more than 20 purpose-built legal skills.
  • In Word desktop, the legal plugin is enabled by default. When enabled, Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks in Word.
  • In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before Copilot can use legal skills to complete legal tasks.
  • The legal skills can help users review contracts against playbooks, draft contracts using templates and precedent agreements, compare contracts with precedents, templates, and policies, and explain tracked changes.
  • The Legal Agent is being retired. Existing Legal Agent users will lose access to the product.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin setup is required.

If your organization plans to use the legal plugins:

  • Ensure Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses are assigned to eligible users.
  • Review internal legal workflows that may benefit from these capabilities.
  • Communicate these capabilities to your legal teams.
  • Update internal documentation or help desk guidance as appropriate.
  • Instruct legal team users to add the legal plugin in Cowork.
  • Instruct legal team users to use legal skills in Copilot in Word desktop.

If your organization does not plan to use the legal plugins:

  • Turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center to disable the legal plugin in Word for all users.
  • Turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center to disable the plugin in Cowork for all users.

Learn more

  • Manage Copilot for legal - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. The legal plugins can use work context from Microsoft 365 to support legal tasks. The supplied source does not specify changes to data storage or caching.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Legal capabilities previously released as the Legal Agent are being made available as legal plugins in Word and Cowork. They provide purpose-built legal skills and can use work context from Microsoft 365.
Does the change provide users a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can use purpose-built legal skills in Copilot in Word and Cowork to summarize, draft, review, and redline legal documents.
Does the change add integration with third-party software products?Yes. The legal plugins can connect to supported third-party legal sources. The supplied sources do not identify specific third-party products.
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can turn off Legal Skills in M365 Copilot in Word in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center and turn off the Cowork for Legal plugin in the Microsoft 365 admin center. The supplied source does not specify whether these controls support Entra ID group membership.
Does the change allow a user to enable or disable the feature themselves?Yes. In Cowork, users must add the legal plugin before using its legal skills. The supplied source does not state that users can independently disable the Word legal plugin.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot Feedback UX update
item.description:
Updated November 3, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

We’re updating the thumbs-down feedback experience in Microsoft Copilot to make it easier for users to provide specific, actionable feedback. Today, many thumbs-down responses are submitted without comments, providing sentiment but limited information about the issue. When users select thumbs down, they’ll be able to select one or more feedback categories and optionally provide additional comments, giving each categorized response a signal that can be routed to the appropriate team or issue type.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-November 2026 (previously late October) and expect to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously late October).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users who can submit feedback in supported Microsoft Copilot experiences may see the updated thumbs-down feedback form. The planned audience includes users signed in with Microsoft Entra ID organizational accounts, users signed in with consumer Microsoft accounts, and users in Education tenants. The feature isn’t currently planned for Mobile, GCC, GCC High, DoD, or other sovereign cloud environments.

The updated feedback experience is planned for Microsoft Copilot, Copilot in Microsoft Edge, Copilot in Microsoft Outlook, and Copilot in Microsoft Teams, across web browsers, Windows, and macOS. The WXPN/Catalyst experience isn’t currently included.

When a user selects thumbs down on a Copilot response, they may see selectable categories describing the issue, can select more than one category, and can optionally enter additional feedback in a free-text field. The thumbs-up feedback experience isn’t changing. This update applies only to the existing “Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft” admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged. During the controlled rollout, some users will continue to see the existing feedback experience.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required for this change. It will be visible to users who are already allowed to submit feedback under the existing policy.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. When a user chooses to submit thumbs-down feedback, the selected categories, optional free-text comment, and optional screenshot are new data captured as part of that submission.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. This UX change applies to the existing "Allow users to submit feedback to Microsoft" admin policy; all other feedback policy experiences remain unchanged.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Rewrite with Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat coming soon to Edge for Business users
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

Introduction

Microsoft Edge for Business will soon support Writing Assistance, a new feature powered by Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat. This capability helps users draft and rephrase editable text directly within Edge, enhancing productivity and writing quality. Users can access Writing Assistance by highlighting editable text and right-clicking to open the context menu.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 420335.

When this will happen

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling late January 2027 (previously end of October 2026) and expect to complete rollout by late January 2027 (previously late October). 

How this affects your organization

  • Writing Assistance will be enabled by default for Edge for Business users. 
  • Users can access Writing Assistance by highlighting editable text and right-clicking to open the context menu.
  • If Microsoft 365 Copilot is restricted from accessing page content due to Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies, Writing Assistance will not function on that content.
  • Admins can manage this feature using the InlineComposeEnabled policy setting.

What you can do to prepare

No admin action is required before rollout.

We recommend:

  • Reviewing your current DLP configurations to understand how they may impact Writing Assistance functionality.
  • Notifying users about this new capability.
  • Updating internal documentation to reflect this change.

Learn more about how DLP affects Copilot access to page content: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat in Edge and Access to Page Content | Microsoft Edge | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This change introduces a new generative AI capability through Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, allowing users to rewrite or draft text directly in Edge for Business.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot Chat by highlighting editable text and using the right-click context menu to access Writing Assistance, enabling AI-assisted drafting and rephrasing.
Does the change modify Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement?Yes. If DLP policies restrict Copilot from accessing page content, the Writing Assistance feature will not function on that content.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can manage the availability of this feature using the InlineComposeEnabled policy setting.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?Yes. Users can choose to use the Writing Assistance feature by manually invoking it through the right-click context menu in Edge.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated November 9, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Gov rollout of this feature is still paused at this time. We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by late November 2026 (previously early November) via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and November 23, 2026 (previously November 3) for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: We will communicate via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) New Outlook for Windows: All Accounts view brings email into a single inbox view
item.description:
Updated November 6, 2026: Admin controls for All Accounts view (Unified Inbox) are now available. We have added policy configuration guidance below. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

The All Accounts view, also known as Unified Inbox, lets users see email from multiple connected accounts in a single inbox view in the new Outlook for Windows without merging their mailboxes. Each account's inbox stays separate, and All Accounts view brings messages together so users can triage mail from one place.

Users can read, delete, search, move, archive, and mark messages across accounts without switching between mailboxes. The experience integrates with Copilot for AI-assisted email workflows and supports Search with Copilot for finding messages across the user's primary account.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): We began rolling out in late September 2026 and expect to complete by late November 2026 (previously late October).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Users with more than one connected account in the new Outlook for Windows will be able to triage email across accounts from a single All Accounts view. This does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Each account remains separate, and All Accounts view provides a unified view only.

All Accounts view is enabled by default for eligible users. Users can change this setting unless their organization enforces a configuration through the admin policy described below.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required unless you want to manage this experience for your users. 

The policy “Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows” is now available through the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center at config.office.com. Admins can configure whether All Accounts view is enabled or disabled by default and whether users can change that setting. The policy can be applied to selected groups. 

If the policy is not configured, All Accounts view remains enabled by default, and users can turn it off or back on. Admins who want to disable it and prevent users from enabling it must set “Configure the unified inbox view” to Disabled and “Allow user to override this setting” to Disabled. 

To configure the policy: 

  1. Go to config.office.com and open Customization > Policy Management. 
  2. Create or edit a policy configuration and scope it to the group you want to manage. 
  3. Find “Show All Accounts view for users with multiple accounts in Outlook for Windows” and set Configuration setting to Enabled. 
  4. Under “Configure the unified inbox view,” select Enabled to show All Accounts view by default, or Disabled to keep account inboxes separate by default. 
  5. Under “Allow user to override this setting,” select Enabled to let users change the configured behavior, or Disabled to prevent changes. 
  6. Review and publish the policy configuration.

[Compliance considerations:]

This feature provides a unified view across connected accounts in the new Outlook for Windows but does not merge mailboxes or move messages between accounts. Review your organization's Outlook account and automated-assistance policies as appropriate.

item.title: [planForChange] Action required: Update permissions for Exchange Online Admin API
item.description:

This change provides a clearer permission model for applications accessing Exchange Online administrative endpoints and supports the ongoing modernization of Exchange Online administration, including migration from Exchange Web Services (EWS).

The Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 endpoints are not being retired. Only the permissions used to access them are changing:

  • Exchange.ManageV2 is being replaced by Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage.
  • Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 is being replaced by Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp.

Applications using the affected permissions must transition to the corresponding new permissions to maintain uninterrupted access.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: New permissions become available November 1, 2026. Complete migration by November 30, 2026. Existing permissions are deprecated December 1, 2026.
  • GCC, GCC High, DoD: Rollout begins in November 2026, with existing permissions deprecated January 1, 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

This change affects organizations that develop, own, or manage applications accessing Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 using Exchange.ManageV2 for delegated access or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 for application-only access. If your organization does not use either permission, no action is required.

Platforms/Services:

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange Online Admin API v2.0
  • Microsoft Entra application permission and consent configuration

What will happen:

  • Applications must transition to Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage or Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp, as applicable.
  • Administrators must grant consent to the new permissions where required.
  • Existing Exchange Online RBAC requirements continue to apply.
  • Exchange Online Admin API v2.0 endpoint URLs, API version, and supported operations are not changing as a result of this update.
  • Applications relying exclusively on the retired permissions after the applicable deprecation date will no longer be able to access the APIs.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  1. Identify affected applications. Review applications using Exchange.ManageV2 or Exchange.ManageAsAppV2.
  2. Configure the new permissions. Add the corresponding Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage or Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp permission.
  3. Grant administrator consent. Ensure the required new permissions are approved.
  4. Verify Exchange RBAC assignments. Confirm that the application or delegated user has the necessary Exchange roles.
  5. Validate API functionality. Test affected workflows using the new permissions before removing the existing permissions.
  6. Remove the retired permissions. After successful validation, remove the old permissions from the application configuration.
  7. Update explicit permission references. Update configurations, scripts, or consent workflows that reference the existing permission names.
  8. Check third-party applications. Contact your application provider to determine whether an update is required.

For more information, see Authentication and authorization for the Exchange Online Admin API.

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads
item.description:
Update: Release of this feature has been postponed; we will announce a new date in the future.

We are announcing the ability to use role-based enforcement for recording and transcription downloads in Dynamics 365 Contact Center.

How does this affect me?
This feature helps organizations better protect sensitive customer communications by separating permissions to view recordings and transcripts from permissions to download them. Admins can assign new Dataverse security roles to prevent selected users from downloading recordings or transcripts while still allowing them to view and play back content as permitted by existing access.

The two new Dataverse security roles that will be available are:
  • Deny Recording Download
  • Deny Transcription Download
When either role is assigned to a user:
  • The user can continue to view and play back recordings and transcripts as permitted by existing access.
  • The user is blocked from downloading the corresponding artifact.
Enforcement of these models is applied server-side across the Dynamics 365 Contact Center UI, public and internal APIs, and direct download URLs or integrations. Download requests will also be denied regardless of how they are initiated.

Access control is driven entirely by Dataverse role assignment. The deny roles override implicit download behavior without affecting recording, transcription, or playback functionality.

These controls help reduce the risk of unauthorized data export, support compliance and data governance requirements, and allow organizations to maintain operational visibility without allowing data removal.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

item.title: [planForChange] Work IQ expands memory capabilities to agents
item.description:
[What and why]

A new Work IQ MCP path, /memory/me/coreMemories, gives authorized agents access to a user’s memory profile. This profile enables agents to provide more personalized and relevant assistance. At launch, it includes Custom Instructions, Saved Memories, and memories derived from chat history. The memory profile will continue to evolve and improve over time.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by late December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users whose agents have access to the Work IQ MCP server and whose applicable personalization settings allow the relevant information to be included in their memory profile

Platforms and services

  • Work IQ MCP
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

A new /memory/me/coreMemoriespath in Work IQ MCP will provide a memory profile for the authenticated user.

The path supports only the fetch tool. Memory cannot be written or modified through Work IQ MCP.

Only the authenticated user’s memory profile is available. A user’s memory profile is not shared with other users.

Work IQ MCP has a new policy that controls access to memory through Work IQ MCP at Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies. Like other read policies, this policy is enabled by default.

If Enhanced personalization is disabled, Copilot Memory is disabled and is not available through the MCP path.

  • User personalization settings in Copilot Chat > Settings > Personalization are respected:If Customize Copilot is disabled, Custom Instructions are not included in the memory profile.
  • If Saved memories is disabled, saved memories are not included in the memory profile.
  • If Chat history & work insights is disabled, insights from chat history and Microsoft 365 activity are not included in the memory profile.

Changes to the Enhanced personalization control and to the user settings may take up to 48 hours to take effect.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required.

Admins who want to manage access to memory through Work IQ MCP can review the memory read policy at Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Work IQ MCP has a memory read policy under Microsoft 365 Admin center > Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policies. The policy is enabled by default.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot Chat: Planner Agent task assignment, catch-up, and Copilot memory integration
item.description:
[What and why]

We are expanding Planner Agent in Microsoft Copilot Chat with task assignment, scheduled task catch-up, and Copilot memory integration. These improvements help users manage tasks and shared plans, identify outstanding work, and receive personalized responses. We are also improving support for larger plans, response quality, speed, and reliability.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by early December 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with an active Microsoft Copilot license who have access to Planner Agent. Administrators can manage Planner Agent availability through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot on the web
  • Microsoft Copilot in Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft Planner

What will happen

Task assignment

  • Users can assign tasks to one or more people in shared basic plans, including assigning multiple tasks at once.
  • Users can reassign or remove assignees, view tasks grouped by person, and review proposed changes before saving them.

Scheduled task catch-up

  • Users can identify outstanding work, commitments, and items awaiting their input based on recent emails, chats, and meetings.
  • Users can generate suggestions on demand or configure recurring schedules with optional email notifications when suggestions are ready for review.
  • Suggested tasks include their sources and remain editable drafts until users save them to Planner. Users can modify, pause, or delete their schedules.

Copilot memory

  • Planner Agent can personalize responses using saved memories and preferences inferred from previous Copilot chats.
  • Users can save, update, or delete memories through Planner Agent and review, delete, or turn off memories in Copilot personalization settings.

Additional improvements

  • Users can create plans without the previous 30-task limit and receive more complete responses for complex plans.
  • Model selection, improved grounding in Microsoft 365 content, and performance enhancements provide more flexible, reliable responses.
  • Users can find Planner Agent under Agents & Skills, pin it, or invoke it using @Planner Agent in Copilot chats.

Limitations and default behavior

  • Planner Agent supports personal tasks and shared basic plans, but not premium plans. It cannot delete tasks or undo changes.
  • These improvements are enabled by default for users with access to Planner Agent. Users can run task catch-up on demand or configure recurring schedules. No recurring schedule is created automatically.
  • AI-generated tasks, plans, and updates, including task assignments, remain drafts until users review and confirm them.
  • Planner Agent uses only content that the signed-in user already has permission to access in Microsoft 365.

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that users have an active Microsoft Copilot license.
  • Review Planner Agent access settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Inform users about the new capabilities, including optional scheduled task catch-up.
  • Update internal documentation and training materials.
  • Pin Planner Agent for easier access through Agents > All agents > Manage pinned agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Pinning requires the AI Administrator role and can take up to six hours to appear.

  • Manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center | Microsoft Learn
  • What is Planner Agent in Copilot? | Microsoft Support

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will be generally available by November 30, 2026.

How does this affect me?
Users will be able to configure natural-language playbooks to automatically manage conversation priority, overflow handling, representative assignment, and routing as conditions change throughout the conversation lifecycle.

Key capabilities will include:
  • Dynamic priority escalation: Adjust priority based on wait time, queue transfers, customer tier, and other conditions.
  • Overflow handling: Trigger callbacks, route conversations to alternate queues, expand assignment eligibility, notify supervisors, or send contextual customer messages when defined conditions occur, including for direct inward dial calls.
  • Preferred representative assignment: Reconnect customers with previously engaged or preferred representatives when available and within capacity, with fallback to another qualified representative.
  • Bullseye routing: Expand the pool of eligible representatives over time based on skills, proficiency, teams, or other criteria.
Users will configure playbooks through guided templates with built-in validation to identify conflicts before publication. Publishing a playbook will consume Copilot credits. No Copilot credits will be consumed during runtime when playbooks process conversations.

Existing customers can continue using their current conversation orchestration playbooks, and new customers can create playbooks.

What action do I need to take?
Users will need to enable the conversation orchestration toggle to use this capability. Enabling the toggle will not consume Copilot credits.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Orchestrate conversation distribution with natural language playbooks.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Contact Center - Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability by November 6, 2026.

How does this affect me?
This feature introduces a tiered assignment strategy that automatically expands the pool of eligible customer service representatives as conversation wait times increase. Admins can configure a bullseye routing playbook, allowing them to associate user groups with a queue and define wait time thresholds for each tier they add to that queue. Once configured, conversation orchestration monitors each conversation's wait time and automatically expands the eligible pool when thresholds are reached.

What action do I need to take?
Admins can enable bullseye routing under conversation orchestration to start configuring bullseye playbooks. If you’re already using bullseye routing under conversation orchestration, you can continue using your existing configurations without additional action.

Copilot credits are used only when an admin publishes a playbook, which makes the configured orchestration logic active for use. Once published, the playbook can process any number of customer conversations without consuming additional Copilot credits. Saving a playbook as a draft or simply enabling Conversation Orchestration does not consume Copilot credits.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Use bullseye routing with user groups to orchestrate conversations.
